# FindMyDoctor Project Schedule

This schedule follows Section 3.2, Project Schedules, in the SPMP. The SPMP describes a recommended 9-week prototype delivery baseline and allows parallel work where dependencies and staffing permit.

**Progress status:** Weeks 1–5 are marked done as requested, and Week 6 is in progress. This status is a project progress marker and is not an independent verification of each deliverable.

**Invoice note:** The invoice generated by the system is a prototype payment receipt, not an official receipt. The PDF carries this label.

**Settings note:** The Secretary and Doctor Settings page redesigns both include Change password (built outside the weekly plan). On the Secretary page, the "Invoice details" and "GCash account details" cards are "Coming soon" placeholders until Weeks 7 and 8.

**Completed outside the weekly plan:** The Doctor, Secretary, and Admin dashboard redesigns, the admin audit log, doctor deactivation, and secretary invite resend and password reset are complete. The web session redesign (role-scoped sessions, Remember Me, trusted browsers) is implemented.

| Week | Primary activities | Exit evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1–3 | Initiation, architecture, authentication, RBAC, OTP flows, doctor approval, admin provisioning, and web dashboards. | Approved baselines, role-protection tests, admin seed, and protected routes. | Done |
| Week 4 | Scheduling module (working hours, availability, break periods), capacity calculation (30-minute default), daily capacity configuration, and reservation system foundation. | Capacity calculation tests, schedule CRUD operations, and basic reservation tests. | Done |
| Week 5 | Unified queue management with sequential numbering, concurrency-safe queue assignment, automatic queue reassignment on cancellation with notifications, capacity enforcement across online and walk-in registrations, walk-in registration with temporary password generation, doctor-specific patient record check before booking, and mobile navigation to appointments view. | Booking/queue integration tests, conflict prevention tests, walk-in account lifecycle tests, concurrency-safe queue assignment tests, queue reassignment notification tests, and doctor-specific patient record validation tests. | Done |
| Week 6 | GCash payment flow (static QR code, receipt upload, verification states), additional charges, payment verification, and secretary-patient chat (conversation authorization and messaging). Payment total equals consultation fee plus additional charges. Walk-in patients may pay after consultation with secretary confirmation. Receipt upload never auto-marks payment as Paid (statuses: Unpaid, Pending Verification, Paid, Rejected). Notifications triggered for new secretary messages and payment verification using the notification module. | Payment state tests, receipt verification workflow, chat authorization tests, private receipt storage verification, total-amount calculation tests, and a test that patient-to-doctor messaging is blocked. | In progress |
| Week 7 | Records and prescriptions (first): consultation/visit records, medical history, prescription management, and PDF generation. A visit links to an appointment; a prescription contains items (medication, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions). Prescription-availability notification; patient access limited to their own prescriptions and PDFs. Medicine billing and invoices (built sequentially after prescriptions): (1) MEDICINE charge lines on the visit bill with name, quantity, and unit price, optionally linked to a prescription item, priced by the secretary and never by the doctor; medicines the clinic does not stock are prescribed but not charged; no inventory tracking in the prototype. (2) Cash or GCash payment method, with cash confirmed directly by the secretary and neither method auto-marking Paid. (3) Balance handling when an advance payment was already made. (4) Invoice PDF with an invoice number, generated only when payment status is Paid, stored privately, labeled as a prototype payment receipt; paid invoices are voided and reissued, never edited. (5) Invoice chat message type and a "Send to patient" action on the secretary web dashboard, with the patient notification created and an authorized, short-lived signed-URL download endpoint; the mobile display and download screens are delivered in Week 8. (6) Secretary Settings "Invoice details" (clinic name, address, contact number, footer line) replaces its "Coming soon" placeholder and feeds the invoice PDF header and footer. (7) Dashboard hookups: the Doctor dashboard "Needs a record" section shows completed consultations without a visit record or prescription, and the Secretary dashboard "Payments needing action" section includes Paid visits whose invoice has not been sent. Parallel track: AI chatbot integration (safety and data minimization, identifier redaction, redacted logging, backend-only key handling, patient-only access, free-tier controls, missing-key behavior, doctor lookup, and mobile AI UI) completed with all tests passing. | Role-based end-to-end workflow tests, mobile feature integration tests, end-to-end test for schedule-change flow (exception/break change affecting active appointments -> confirmation -> affected-patient notification, with no auto-cancellation), a check that the Secretary dashboard "Schedule alerts" section lists changes awaiting confirmation, end-to-end test for waitlist, end-to-end test for cancel/reschedule, end-to-end test for the billing flow (prescribe -> add medicine charges -> pay -> verify -> invoice -> chat -> patient download), a test that the GCash account name and number saved in Settings appear in the mobile payment screen, and a check that ADMIN cannot perform clinic operations (schedules, capacity, queue, payments, invoices, consultation records). | In progress |
| Week 8 | Mobile integration with appointments, queue, history, prescriptions, and notifications; end-to-end role workflows. Waitlist feature (join waitlist and waitlist status notifications), patient cancel and reschedule of eligible appointments in mobile app, patient payments view (GCash QR and receipt upload) with invoice list and download, invoice messages in the patient chat thread with download, Secretary Settings "GCash account details" (account name and GCash number) replacing its "Coming soon" placeholder and shown beside the QR code in the mobile payment screen, and patient queue visibility. Notifications: appointment changes (cancel/reschedule), prescription availability, invoice availability (displayed in the mobile app), waitlist updates, and notices to affected patients after a confirmed secretary/doctor exception or break-period change. The Secretary dashboard "Schedule alerts" section is connected to the schedule-change confirmation flow. Notification module foundation exists from earlier weeks. | Role-based end-to-end workflow tests, mobile feature integration tests, end-to-end test for schedule-change flow (exception/break change affecting active appointments -> confirmation -> affected-patient notification, with no auto-cancellation), a check that the Secretary dashboard "Schedule alerts" section lists changes awaiting confirmation, end-to-end test for waitlist, end-to-end test for cancel/reschedule, end-to-end test for the billing flow (prescribe -> add medicine charges -> pay -> verify -> invoice -> chat -> patient download), a test that the GCash account name and number saved in Settings appear in the mobile payment screen, and a check that ADMIN cannot perform clinic operations (schedules, capacity, queue, payments, invoices, consultation records). | Not started |
| Week 9 | Regression testing, performance/concurrency checks, privacy/security review, defect resolution, UAT, deployment, release notes, and handover. Asia/Manila timezone consistency check across appointments, queue entries, schedules, messages, notifications, payments, and invoices. Privacy/security review to confirm Supabase service role key and AI keys stay backend-only, receipts and invoices are not publicly accessible, and mobile/web never access PostgreSQL directly. Deployment as mobile and web clients reaching the backend API over HTTPS. | Timezone consistency results, security review findings, release candidate, UAT approval, and approved prototype release. | Not started |
